title: Meetings that end with decisions

audience.who: corporate employees who run or attend recurring team and project meetings
audience.knows: how meetings work; has sat through many that ended without a clear outcome
audience.cares_about: less time lost in meetings, knowing what was agreed and who does what next

outcome: Run your next meeting so it ends with each decision written down with an owner and a date before people leave.
through_line: A meeting ends with decisions only when you design for them at three points: before (name the decision it must make), during (keep the talk on it and say how it gets decided), and at the close (read back who does what by when, then put it in writing).

arc_plan.what: A familiar meeting: an hour of good discussion, everyone leaves, and nobody can say what was decided or who does what.
arc_plan.source_anchor: requester notes: practical how-to for working adults

arc_plan.what: Three practical moves, before, during and at the close, that turn the same meeting into one that ends with decisions.
Before: name the decision the meeting must make, as a question in the invite, and invite the people who own it.
During: keep the talk on the decision, park side topics, and say how the decision will be made and by whom.
Close: read each decision back with an owner and a date, then send it in writing.
The viewer judges a meeting's closing notes: which line is a real decision with owner and date, and which is only a topic discussed.
The opening meeting replayed with the three moves: it ends on a short written list of decisions, owners and dates.
arc_plan.source_anchor: requester notes: practical how-to for working adults

must_cover.what: Invite the people needed to make the decision

must_cover.what: Keep the discussion on that decision; park off-topic items for later
must_cover.source_anchor: topic research: knowledge sheet (P2), to be confirmed

must_cover.what: Make clear how the decision will be made and who makes it

must_cover.what: Close by reading back each decision with an owner and a due date
must_cover.source_anchor: topic research: knowledge sheet (P2), to be confirmed

must_cover.what: Send the decisions and actions in writing soon after the meeting

must_avoid: statistics about meetings without a source (for example hours wasted per week)
invented sayings attributed to real people
theory of meetings or decision science; practical how-to steps only
opening by explaining what a meeting is, or with a list of contents
example_posture: One running example: a recurring project team meeting at an ordinary company, run by one person; the lesson returns to it from the hook to the payoff.
visual_direction: A trainer's whiteboard in one marker colour: simple people and props sketched as the narration needs them, one board built up by additions, the three moves as a short list that grows, a before and after of the meeting's closing notes.
voice_note: A capable colleague who has sat through too many meetings: brisk and practical, no lecturing, no jargon.
open_questions: Topic mode: every must_cover entry waits on the fact-finder's knowledge sheet; any entry the research cannot ground is dropped.
